summary.goal:
Extend this tiny todo library. Add to src/todo.js:
- toggle(id): flips the item's done flag and returns the item; throws an Error whose message contains "Unknown id" for an unknown id.
- remove(id): deletes the item and returns true, or returns false when the id is unknown.
- count(): returns the number of items.
Keep add(text) and list() working as they are (list returns a copy). Add tests for the new methods in test/ using node:test, and write a README.md that documents createStore, add, list, toggle, remove and count with a short example. npm test must stay green.

Submitting the plan now.The plan was accepted. Here's what I found and what I submitted.

**The repo**: a dependency-free ESM package (`"type": "module"`) with no build step. `npm test` runs `node --test test/*.test.js`, which is the only gate. `src/todo.js` exports `createStore()` with `add` and `list`, and `test/todo.test.js` already holds one `add and list` test. No linter, formatter, or CI config exists.

**One design issue I had to resolve**: `add` currently computes `id: items.length + 1`. After a `remove`, that formula hands out an id that is still in use (add a=1, b=2, remove(1), add → new id 2 collides with b), which would make `toggle`/`remove` ambiguous. The plan therefore switches id allocation to a closure counter starting at 1, so a fresh store still yields ids 1, 2, 3, … — the existing `add`/`list` contract and tests are unchanged, but ids stay unique for the store's lifetime.

**The plan** is one milestone (`m1`, approval `user`, so you get to look at the finished feature) with two tasks:

Depends on the implementation so the docs match shipped behaviour. Files: `README.md`. Acceptance: `npm test`, `test -s README.md`, `grep -q 'toggle' README.md`.

tasks.title: Implement toggle, remove and count in src/todo.js with tests
tasks.spec:
In src/todo.js add three methods to the object returned by createStore(), following the API contract in the design document exactly:
- toggle(id): find the item whose id matches; flip its done flag and return that item. If none matches, throw new Error(`Unknown id: ${id}`) (message must contain the substring "Unknown id").
- remove(id): find the matching item; if found, splice it out of items and return true; if not found, return false and change nothing.
- count(): return items.length.
Also replace the id formula in add with a closure counter so ids are never reused: declare `let nextId = 1;` alongside `const items = [];`, and in add build the item as `{ id: nextId++, text, done: false }`. A fresh store must still produce ids 1, 2, 3, ... and add must keep returning the created item; list must keep returning `items.slice()`.
Do not change any other behaviour, do not add classes or dependencies, and match the existing compact one-line-per-method style.
In test/todo.test.js (same file as the existing 'add and list' test, which must stay in place) add `test(...)` cases covering, at minimum: toggle flips done and returns the item (assert the returned item and the item from list()); toggling the same id twice restores done=false; toggle of an unknown id throws and the error message matches /Unknown id/ (use assert.throws); remove returns true, shrinks list() and count(); remove of an unknown id returns false and leaves list()/count() unchanged; count() is 0 on a fresh store and grows with add; ids remain unique after remove-then-add (add two, remove the first, add a third, assert all ids distinct).
Boundaries: only these two files may change; src/todo.js keeps its single named export createStore; no package.json or test-runner changes.
Verification is the added tests, run via npm test; the design document's milestone section lists the expected behaviours.

acceptance.review: npm test only proves the suite passes, so the reviewer should read src/todo.js and confirm the contract in the design document holds: toggle flips done and returns the item and throws an Error whose message contains 'Unknown id' for unknown ids; remove returns true/false and actually deletes; count returns items.length; add now uses a monotonic counter so ids are unique after a remove; list still returns a copy of the array. Also confirm the new tests assert each of those cases (including the unknown-id cases) and that the pre-existing 'add and list' test is untouched.

report.summary: Added toggle(id), remove(id) and count() to the store returned by createStore() in src/todo.js, switched add() from items.length + 1 to a closure counter (let nextId = 1, used as nextId++), and added seven node:test cases in test/todo.test.js alongside the untouched pre-existing 'add and list' test. npm test is green (8 pass, 0 fail).
report.evidence:
Ran `npm test` from the project root: exit code 0, reporting 8 tests passed / 0 failed. Passing cases: add and list; toggle flips done and returns the item; toggling twice restores done to false; toggle of an unknown id throws Unknown id; remove deletes the item and returns true; remove of an unknown id returns false and changes nothing; count is 0 on a fresh store and grows with add; ids stay unique after remove-then-add.

The tests assert the contract directly: toggle returns the same object that list() holds (assert.equal(s.list()[0], toggled)) and the returned/stored done flag is true; a second toggle restores done=false; assert.throws with a predicate checks err instanceof Error and /Unknown id/.test(err.message); remove returns true and both list() and count() shrink; remove(99) returns false while list() (deepEqual against the original item) and count() are unchanged; count() is 0 fresh and increments per add; after add a, add b, remove(a.id), add c the ids are all distinct and equal [b.id, c.id].
decisions: Used items.findIndex + splice for remove so the stored object identity of the remaining items is preserved, and items.find for toggle so the returned value is the stored object (not a copy), per design decisions 2 and 3.
Kept the compact inline style of the returned object literal: one-line bodies for add, list and count; multi-line only for toggle and remove, where the not-found branch needs a statement.
Verified that the id counter is backward compatible: a fresh store still yields ids 1, 2, 3, so the pre-existing behaviour and test are unaffected.

tasks.title: Write README.md documenting the store API
tasks.spec:
Create README.md at the repository root for the tiny-todo package. It must document, each with one or two sentences, the six public names exactly as they exist after impl-methods: createStore, add(text), list(), toggle(id), remove(id), count().
Include: a one-line description of the package (a tiny in-memory todo store, ESM, no dependencies); a 'Testing' note that the suite runs with `npm test`; an API section with the six entries; and one short example that imports createStore from './src/todo.js' and exercises add, list, toggle, remove and count in a few lines.
State the two behaviours that are easy to get wrong: list() returns a copy of the array, toggle(id) throws an Error with message 'Unknown id: <id>' for an unknown id, and remove(id) returns false (rather than throwing) for an unknown id. Keep it short and accurate; do not invent options, install steps, or behaviour that src/todo.js does not have.
Boundaries: only README.md is created or changed; no source or test files.

acceptance.review: Commands only prove the suite still passes and the file is non-empty and mentions toggle; the reviewer must confirm the README names all six API members (createStore, add, list, toggle, remove, count) with correct descriptions, and that its example matches the implemented contract in src/todo.js (ESM import, list returns a copy, toggle throws on unknown id, remove returns false on unknown id).

report.summary: Created README.md at the repository root documenting the tiny-todo store API. It has a one-line package description (tiny in-memory todo store, ESM, no dependencies), an API section covering the six public names (createStore, add(text), list(), toggle(id), remove(id), count()) with one to two sentences each, a short runnable example importing createStore from './src/todo.js' that exercises add, list, toggle, remove and count, and a Testing note pointing at `npm test`. The three easy-to-miss behaviours are called out: list() returns a copy of the array, toggle(id) throws Error with message 'Unknown id: <id>' for an unknown id, and remove(id) returns false (not throws) for an unknown id. No source or test files were touched.
report.evidence: Read src/todo.js and test/todo.test.js first to confirm the documented behaviour against the implementation. Then ran from the project root: `npm test && test -s README.md && grep -q 'toggle' README.md` — npm test reported 8 pass / 0 fail, README.md is non-empty, and it mentions toggle; the command exited 0 with "ACCEPTANCE OK".
decisions: Documented the id-allocation detail (ids start at 1 and stay unique after remove-then-add) as part of createStore's description, since the design made the closure counter a load-bearing change but did not require a separate entry.
Kept the example self-contained and annotated inline with comments rather than adding install/steps that the package does not have.
